Breakfast. Travel from Cusco to Puno on a Turismo Avalos coach, stopping at historic sites and mountain towns along the way.

In Andahuaylillas, visit the Church of San Pedro Apóstol. Its murals, carved altars and colonial decoration have earned it the nickname “Sistine Chapel of South America.” Next stop at Raqchi, where you can see the remains of the Temple of Viracocha, dwellings and storehouses in the Inca complex.

Stop for lunch in Sicuani. At La Raya Pass, the highest point on the route at around 4,300–4,400 metres, take in views of the mountains and Andean plateaus and browse a small craft market. In Pukara, learn about the pre-Inca culture of the same name.

The coach arrives in Puno at around 18:00. Transfer to the 4-star Casona Plaza or a comparable hotel.

You can take the Titicaca Train in place of the coach for an additional $295 per person. The train runs on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays according to the operator's timetable.

The railway crosses the high Andes, passing through plateaus and valleys. The train has a dining car, a bar car and an observation car. At La Raya, a stop at more than 4,300 metres gives you time to see the surrounding peaks and plains.

A lunch of a starter, main course and dessert is included. Arrive in Puno at around 19:00, then transfer to your hotel and check in. The rate table lists the 3-star Sol Plaza for the 3-star package. The day's itinerary names the 4-star Casona Plaza. We confirm the final hotel at booking.
